title: Impeachment court summons BOC official, Carpio business partner
summary: The Senate impeachment court has subpoenaed a Bureau of Customs (BOC) official and a former co-owner of Cale88 Foods Corp. to testify on the company’s business operations and export records…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court has subpoenaed a Bureau of Customs (BOC) official and a former co-owner of Cale88 Foods Corp. to testify on the company’s business operations and export records when proceedings on the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte resume on Dec. 1.?
Impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol said subpoenas were issued on Nov. 25 and served on both witnesses on Nov. 26 ahead of the hearings from Dec. 1 to 4.

The witnesses are Customs Deputy Commissioner for assessment and operations coordinating group Agaton Teodoro Uvero and Dr. Lourdes Tingson-Lebosada, who is also the Vice President’s dentist.?Uvero is expected to testify on Cale88 Foods’ exportation records held by the BOC and identify documents concerning the company’s registration and shipments.

On the other hand, Lebosada, who previously co-owned Cale88 with Duterte’s husband Manases Carpio, was directed to testify on the company’s organizational structure, government registrations, business operations, finances, ownership and transactions.
Both witnesses were ordered to appear at 10 a.m. on the scheduled hearing dates and submit three certified true copies and electronic copies of the required records in three USB flash drives.?

Tongol said the respondent’s initial list of two witnesses satisfies the minimum requirement for the resumption of hearings on Dec. 1. Any additional witnesses for the Dec. 2 to 4 hearings must comply with an earlier order requiring five days’ advance notice and at least two witnesses for each hearing day.

The court will automatically reproduce documents submitted in compliance with the subpoenas and furnish copies to both the prosecution and defense panels, subject to restrictions on records covered by statutory confidentiality.
The impeachment court is set to resume proceedings on Dec. 1 at 10 a.m., while exhibit marking continues before the Clerk of Court.?Witness lineup
Meanwhile, the House prosecution panel wants the full lineup of the defense’s witness list after only two names have so far been identified.
House prosecutor and Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon hoped that the defense would provide a clearer picture of its remaining presentation.
“We will give them the chance to have that full witness list. However, there is none yet,” he said.
“Hopefully they can present new witnesses, particularly to fill in the missing details sought by senator-judges pertaining to Cale88,” the lawmaker added.
House lead prosecutor and Batangas 2nd district Rep. Gerville Luistro, for her part, urged the defense to just come clean.

“If there really are more witnesses, reveal them, and if there are none, be transparent to the impeachment court so that the impeachment court can strategize how to wrap up, how to conclude in a timely manner,” she said in a radio interview. — Daphne Galvez
